lines.en: In my family, we always gather on Fridays for a big lunch, and everyone brings a different dish.
Traditions give us a sense of belonging, especially when we are far away from home.
During Ramadan, the streets are decorated with lanterns, and families invite each other to break the fast.
When I visited Japan, I was surprised to learn that people take off their shoes before entering a home.
Some customs have changed over the years, but the most important values are still the same.
It is polite to bring a small gift when you are invited to someone's house, although it is not required.
My grandmother taught me how to bake traditional bread, and I hope to teach my children one day.
Travelling teaches you that there is no single right way to live, only different ways of seeing the world.
Young people today often mix old traditions with new ideas, and I think that is a healthy balance.
Learning about another culture helps us understand each other better and avoid unnecessary misunderstandings.
